headline: Jeff Bezos predicts that AI-driven productivity will mean households no longer need two earners, and some people could work three days a week.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score; the quotes are confirmed, but it is a forecast and the interview was on the evening of 7 Oct.
importance_line: Working families are the people affected if productivity gains turn into shorter weeks or single incomes, but this is a billionaire's forecast, not a finding, and so far the data show only modest AI effects on jobs.
source: Business Insider, citing a Fox News interview
summary: Business Insider reports that Amazon founder Jeff Bezos told Fox News on Wednesday evening, 7 Oct 2026, that AI will raise productivity enough that "you're not going to need to have a two-earner income household", which he thinks could make hiring harder for companies. The outlet adds that fears of mass AI job losses have not yet shown in US data, where unemployment has stayed between 4.1% and 4.5% for two years.
notes: Interview on the evening of 7 Oct (US); first reported on 8 Oct, so kept at the pool score.
